why_winner: Variant C (Tactical) has the strongest structure, best plan compliance, and clearest readability — the four-criteria checklist and build-order are both crisp and actionable. Variants A and B cover the emotional and provocative entry points but neither delivers the full practical framework as cleanly. C scores highest on aggregate but its opening hook is functional rather than scroll-stopping.

runner_up_notes.B: B's opening line — 'Most engineers who say they are building AI loops are running expensive spinners.' — is the strongest hook in the set. It names something the audience does but does not realize, which the performance tracker confirms as the highest-engagement pattern. This line should open the revised C draft.
runner_up_notes.A: A's personal 'I spent weeks reading' framing has the most authentic voice but a weaker hook. The final paragraph rhythm ('Not the other way around') is clean and should be retained in spirit.

issues.description: C opens with 'Here is the exact test for whether an AI loop is worth building.' This is functional and direct but does not stop a scroll. The tracker's top pattern is leading with a specific uncomfortable truth rather than a utility promise. The reader has no stakes yet.
issues.action: Open with B's hook ('Most engineers building AI loops are running expensive spinners.') or a close variant, then pivot immediately to the test. Keep all four criteria and build-order from C unchanged.
